issues.title: Pydantic v1 Config class usage
issues.description: The rule requires data validation to use Pydantic v2 with ConfigDict(extra='forbid'), but this code uses Pydantic v1 'class Config' syntax with 'extra = allow' which permits undeclared fields
issues.problematic_code_snippet:

    message_id: str
    position: int
    thought: str | None = None
    tool: str | None = None
    tool_input: str | None = None
    observation: str | None = None

    class Config:
        extra = "allow"  # Pydantic v1 syntax - should use ConfigDict(extra='forbid')

issues.title: Swapped answer price unit values causing incorrect billing calculations
issues.description: In the create_agent_thought method, the answer_unit_price and answer_price_unit values are swapped. The answer_unit_price is initialized to Decimal('0.001') instead of Decimal(0), while answer_price_unit is initialized to Decimal(0) instead of Decimal('0.001'). This mirrors the correct initialization pattern used for message_unit_price and message_price_unit but with reversed values. This will cause incorrect pricing calculations when computing the total cost of agent responses, potentially leading to billing discrepancies or revenue loss.

issues.title: Type mismatch in total_price initialization breaks Decimal arithmetic
issues.description: The total_price field is initialized with integer 0 instead of Decimal(0), creating a type inconsistency. The MessageAgentThought model defines total_price as Mapped[Decimal | None] expecting a Decimal type, and other price fields (message_unit_price, answer_unit_price, etc.) are correctly initialized with Decimal types. This inconsistency will cause type errors during price calculations when the system attempts to perform Decimal arithmetic operations (addition, multiplication) between Decimal and int types, potentially breaking billing computations or causing runtime exceptions.

issues.title: Tool responses replaced with tool inputs in agent history organization
issues.description: In the organize_agent_history method, when building ToolPromptMessage objects, the content is incorrectly populated from tool_inputs dictionary instead of tool_responses dictionary. This means the LLM will receive the tool's input parameters as if they were the tool's output/response. For example, if a tool was called with {"query": "weather in NYC"}, the agent history would show this input dict as the tool's response instead of the actual weather data. This breaks the agent's ability to learn from previous tool executions and will cause incorrect context to be passed to subsequent LLM calls.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #27749 - refactor(models): Refine MessageAgentThought SQLAlchemy typing

structured_output.summary:
This PR moves `MessageAgentThought` from `Base` to the dataclass-style `TypeBase` and adds `Mapped[...]` annotations to every column, using `Decimal` for the pricing fields. Required fields are moved ahead of defaulted ones, `id` and `created_at` become `init=False`, and the integration tests are updated so they stop passing `id`. That model refactor follows the pattern already used elsewhere in `models/model.py` and looks right. `BaseAgentRunner` also gets matching typing updates: `CreatorUserRole.ACCOUNT`, a None-safe append to `thought`, and explicit None handling when decoding `tool_input` and `observation`.

The runner changes add two real regressions that go beyond typing. First, when rebuilding conversation history, each `ToolPromptMessage` is now filled from `tool_inputs` instead of `tool_responses`. On every later turn, the LLM sees the tool's arguments where the tool's output should be. Second, the initial pricing values in `create_agent_thought` are inconsistent: `answer_unit_price` and `answer_price_unit` look swapped. There's also a new `AgentThoughtValidation` Pydantic model that nothing uses. It's written in Pydantic v1 style, and its own comment says the setting is wrong.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The model typing refactor is fine. But the history rebuild now sends the LLM tool inputs where the tool outputs should be, which breaks multi-turn agent conversations. The pricing defaults are also swapped. Both need fixing before merge.

architecture.overview:
`MessageAgentThought` stores one step of an agent run: what the agent thought, which tools it called, the tool inputs and outputs, token use and pricing. `BaseAgentRunner.create_agent_thought` inserts a placeholder row at the start of each step. `save_agent_thought` fills it in later with tool output and LLM usage. `organize_agent_history` reads past thoughts back and rebuilds assistant tool calls plus tool responses as prompt messages for the next LLM call.

This PR moves the model onto `TypeBase` (`MappedAsDataclass` + `DeclarativeBase`), so the constructor now follows dataclass rules: required fields come first, `id` and `created_at` can't be passed in, and pricing fields are typed as `Decimal`. The runner is updated to match. Along the way it also changes how history is rebuilt and which pricing values a new row starts with.
steps: Start with `api/models/model.py` (`MessageAgentThought`). It now extends `TypeBase`, so every column has a `Mapped[...]` type. Required fields (`message_id`, `position`, `created_by_role`, `created_by`) come before defaulted ones, and `id`/`created_at` are `init=False`.
Then read `BaseAgentRunner.create_agent_thought`. It builds the placeholder row with `Decimal` prices and `CreatorUserRole.ACCOUNT`, and now passes `tool_process_data=None` explicitly.
Next is `save_agent_thought`. It appends to `thought` in a None-safe way, and when `llm_usage` is present it overwrites the price and token fields with real values.

Then `organize_agent_history`. It decodes `tool_input` and `observation` into the `tool_inputs` and `tool_responses` dicts, and builds an `AssistantPromptMessage.ToolCall` plus a `ToolPromptMessage` for each tool.
Last, the integration tests in `test_agent_service.py` stop passing `id=`, because the dataclass constructor now generates it.

findings.title: History rebuild sends tool inputs as tool responses
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/core/agent/base_agent_runner.py`, `organize_agent_history` (around line 500-506) builds each `ToolPromptMessage` from `tool_inputs.get(tool, ...)`, but it should use `tool_responses`. Right now past tool outputs in the LLM history are replaced by tool arguments. Change the content back to `tool_responses.get(tool, agent_thought.observation)`. If the value may be a dict or list, serialize it with `json.dumps(..., ensure_ascii=False)` rather than `str()`, and leave string values alone. Add a unit test for `organize_agent_history` with a thought whose `tool_input` and `observation` are JSON dicts keyed by tool name, and assert that the ToolPromptMessage content is the observation value.

findings.title: answer_unit_price / answer_price_unit initial values are swapped
findings.body:
The placeholder row's pricing values are now asymmetric:

::diff{file="api/core/agent/base_agent_runner.py" lines="319-326"}

The message side is set to `unit_price=0` and `price_unit=0.001`. The answer side is the reverse: `unit_price=0.001` and `price_unit=0`. Before this PR all four were `0`. The model's column defaults (`default=Decimal("0.001")` for both `*_price_unit` columns) show the intended pattern: the unit price starts at 0 and the price unit starts at 0.001.

`save_agent_thought` overwrites these fields only when `llm_usage` is passed. Any thought saved without usage (for example, if the LLM call fails after the row is created) stays in the database with a non-zero `answer_unit_price` and a zero `answer_price_unit`. That's wrong billing and cost data for anything that reads these columns.

::suggestion{file="api/core/agent/base_agent_runner.py" lines="325-326"}
            answer_unit_price=Decimal(0),
            answer_price_unit=Decimal("0.001"),

You could also set `total_price=Decimal(0)` so it matches the new `Mapped[Decimal | None]` type.
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/core/agent/base_agent_runner.py` `create_agent_thought` (lines ~319-326), `answer_unit_price` and `answer_price_unit` have swapped values compared with `message_unit_price` and `message_price_unit`. Set `answer_unit_price=Decimal(0)` and `answer_price_unit=Decimal("0.001")` so they match the message fields and the model defaults in `api/models/model.py` (`MessageAgentThought.*_price_unit` default `Decimal("0.001")`). Also change `total_price=0` to `Decimal(0)` so it matches the column type.

findings.title: Unused AgentThoughtValidation model with a misconfigured Pydantic v1 Config
findings.fixPrompt: In `api/core/agent/base_agent_runner.py` lines 52-65, the new `AgentThoughtValidation` Pydantic model is never used, uses the deprecated v1 `class Config`, and sets `extra = "allow"` even though its comment says it should forbid extras. Remove the class and the now-unused `from pydantic import BaseModel` import. If validation really is wanted, use `model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")` and call it in `create_agent_thought` before building `MessageAgentThought`.

findings.title: TypeBase migration follows the established model pattern
findings.body:
The model rewrite matches the conventions other `TypeBase` models in this file already use. For `id`, that's `insert_default` + `default_factory` + `init=False`, the same as at lines 580, 1343 and 1394. Required fields are placed before defaulted ones so the dataclass is valid, `created_at` is `init=False` with a server default, and the `price_unit` columns get a Python default that matches their `server_default`. The test updates that drop `id=` are needed because the constructor no longer accepts it. The None-safe `thought` append in `save_agent_thought` is also a good fix now that `thought` is `str | None`.
